me:2005:q89.title: GATE ME 2005 | Set 1 | Question: 89
me:2005:q89.question:
An un-insulated air conditioning duct of rectangular cross section 1 m x 0.5 m, carrying air at 20$^{\circ}$C with a velocity of 10 m/s, is exposed to an ambient of 30$^{\circ}$C. Neglect the effect of duct construction material. For air in the range of 20-30$^{\circ}$C, data are as follows: thermal conductivity =0.025 W/m.K; viscosity = 18$\mu$Pa.s; Prandtl number =0.73; density = 1.2 $kg/m^{3}$. The laminar flow Nusselt number is 3.4 for constant wall temperature conditions and, for turbulent flow, Nu=0.023 $Re^{0.8}Pr^{0.33}$

The Reynolds number for the flow is

primary.subtopicLabel: Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes

detailed_solution.concept: Heat Transfer - Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \text { Width: } & a=1 \mathrm{m} \\ \text { Depth: } & b=0.5 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ Velocity: $\quad V=10 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ Air temperature $T=20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ Ambient temperature $T_{0}=30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ Properties of air $$\begin{aligned} k &=0.025 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \\ \mu &=1.8 \mathrm{m} \text { Pa.s }=18 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{Pa} . \\ \mathrm{Pr} &=0.73 \\ \rho &=1.2 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}$$ Equivalent length of duct $$\begin{aligned} L &=\frac{4 \times \text{Cross sectional area }}{\text { Perimeter }} \\ &=\frac{4 A}{P}=\frac{4 \times a b}{2(a+b)} \\ &=\frac{4 \times 1 \times 0.5}{2(1+0.5)}=0.667 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ Reynolds number, $$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Re} &=\frac{\rho \mathrm{VL}}{\mu}=\frac{1.2 \times 10 \times 0.667}{18 \times 10^{-6}} \\ &=4.44 \times 10^{5} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2005:q90.question:
An un-insulated air conditioning duct of rectangular cross section 1 m x 0.5 m, carrying air at 20$^{\circ}$C with a velocity of 10 m/s, is exposed to an ambient of 30$^{\circ}$C. Neglect the effect of duct construction material. For air in the range of 20-30$^{\circ}$C, data are as follows: thermal conductivity =0.025 W/m.K; viscosity = 18$\mu$Pa.s; Prandtl number =0.73; density = 1.2 $kg/m^{3}$ . The laminar flow Nusselt number is 3.4 for constant wall temperature conditions and, for turbulent flow, Nu=0.023 $Re^{0.8}Pr^{0.33}$

The heat transfer per metre length of the duct, in watts, is:

primary.subtopicLabel: Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes

detailed_solution.concept: Heat Transfer - Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown:
As $\mathrm{Re}>4000$, the flow is turbulent

Relation for turbulent flow,

$$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Nu} &=0.023 \mathrm{Re}^{0.8} \mathrm{Pr}^{0.33} \\ \frac{h L}{k}&= 0.023 \times\left(4.44 \times 10^{5}\right) 0.8 \\ & \times(0.73)^{0.33} \\ \frac{\mathrm{h} \times 0.667}{0.025}&= 683.173 \\ \text{or} \quad h &=25.60 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$

Surface area of duct,

$$\begin{aligned} A&=2 \times a l+2 \times b l\\ \text{where }\quad l&= length of duct \\ \therefore \quad A &=2 \times 1 \times l+2 \times 0.5 \times l \\ &=(2+1) l=3 l \end{aligned}$$

Rate of heat transfer,

$$\begin{aligned} Q&=h A\left(T_{0}-T\right) \\ Q&=25.60 \times 3 l \times(30-20)\\ \text{or }\quad \frac{Q}{l}&=768 \mathrm{W} \simeq 769 \mathrm{W} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.
